issues.t: Fuel tank can crack from a blocked vent line (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell around the car, fuel drips under the rear, or a check engine light for the evaporative system.
issues.why: Spiders can build webs inside the fuel tank vent line. With the vent blocked, vacuum builds in the tank and can crack it, letting fuel leak. Suzuki recalled the cars in 2014 and again in 2018 for this.
issues.next: If you smell fuel or see a leak, do not drive the car; park it outside away from flames and have it towed. Check your VIN for both recalls.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor may misclassify the occupant (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light does not match who is in the seat, or the airbag warning light comes on.
issues.why: The front passenger seat occupant detection system can fail or misjudge who is sitting there. The airbag might then deploy for a child or stay off for an adult. Suzuki issued two recalls in 2019.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls. Until it is fixed, keep children in the back seat and have the system repaired free at a dealer.

issues.t: Shifter can leave Park without the brake pressed (recall)
issues.sym: The gear selector moves out of Park without your foot on the brake.
issues.why: A fault in the shift lock lets the selector leave Park when the brake is not pressed, so the car could roll unexpectedly.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake when parked and check your VIN for this recall; the repair is free.

issues.t: CVT hesitates, loses power or stops moving
issues.sym: The car lugs at low engine speed, whines or drones, is slow to accelerate, stops shifting, or suddenly will not move.
issues.why: Owners report problems with the automatic CVT (continuously variable transmission), from poor response that a software update helped to complete failures at higher mileage.
issues.next: If the car loses drive, get it out of traffic and stop. Have the transmission codes read and ask a dealer about software updates before agreeing to a replacement.

issues.t: CVT control module can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly slows down or will not accelerate normally.
issues.why: On 2013 Kizashis with the CVT, the transmission control module can fail and cut speed or acceleration.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Dealers replace the module free of charge.

issues.t: Dash storage door can open in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom. The door might swing open in a crash.
issues.why: An instrument panel storage door on some early 2010 cars may not stay shut in a collision, which could injure occupants.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall; the repair is free at a Suzuki dealer.

issues.t: Power steering cuts out
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, or feels loose or vague.
issues.why: Owners report the power steering going out at random. The Kizashi uses electric power steering, so a fault in its motor, control module or wiring can switch the assist off.
issues.next: If the steering gets heavy, slow down and steer with both hands; you can still steer, it just takes more effort. Have the steering codes read before driving far.

issues.t: Push-button start will not crank or steering stays locked
issues.sym: You press the start button and nothing happens, the dash says to turn the wheel to release the lock, the key fob is not recognized, or the engine stalls soon after starting.
issues.why: The electronic steering lock, its module or the keyless start system can fail. One owner reports a $645 steering lock module repair.
issues.next: Try turning the wheel while pressing the button, and try a fresh fob battery. If it keeps happening, have the keyless start and steering lock systems checked.

issues.t: Headlight bulbs burn out often and are hard to reach
issues.sym: One low beam goes dark, often again and again, and the bulb is very hard to change.
issues.why: Burned-out headlight bulbs are the most reported Kizashi problem. On many cars part of the front bumper cover has to come off to reach them.
issues.next: Do not drive at night with one headlight. Replace bulbs in pairs, and expect a shop to charge mostly labor.

issues.t: Coolant leaks and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant on the ground or dried on the radiator fans, a dropping coolant level, the A/C cutting out, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: Owners report leaks from the coolant tank and cooling pipes, plus water pump and thermostat failures.
issues.next: If the gauge climbs toward hot, pull over and shut the engine off. Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak.

issues.t: Drive belt pulley or tensioner failure
issues.sym: Squealing, a belt that slips or comes off, a battery light, and fast overheating.
issues.why: A seized pulley or a weak belt tensioner can let the accessory belt slip or break, which stops the water pump and alternator.
issues.next: If the belt breaks, stop driving before the engine overheats. Have the belt, tensioner and pulleys checked together.

issues.t: Oil leak from pressure sender or gasket
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning-oil smell, or oil on the drive belt.
issues.why: Owners report oil leaks from the oil pressure sending unit and from engine gaskets. Oil reaching the belt can make it slip.
issues.next: Check the oil level often until it is fixed and have the leak traced. Clean oil off the belt area so the belt does not slip.

issues.t: Worn shocks or struts
issues.sym: A bouncy or floaty ride, clunks over bumps, or leaking shocks.
issues.why: Shock absorbers and struts are the second most reported Kizashi repair in owner surveys.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected and replace shocks in pairs on the same axle.

issues.t: Engine mount failure
issues.sym: A rattle or clunk from the front when accelerating or shifting, or extra vibration in the cabin.
issues.why: Owners report engine mounts wearing out, sometimes early.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked. A broken mount strains hoses, wiring and other mounts.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensors leak or corrode
issues.sym: The tire pressure light stays on or flashes, or a tire slowly loses air at the valve stem.
issues.why: The tire pressure sensors built into the valve stems can corrode, crack or leak air.
issues.next: Check all tire pressures with a gauge first. A shop can replace the leaking sensor and relearn it to the car.

issues.t: Check engine light from EVAP canister or gas cap
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes for an evaporative system leak.
issues.why: A loose gas cap or a failed fuel vapor canister can set an evaporative system code.
issues.next: Tighten the gas cap until it clicks and see if the light goes out after a few days of driving. If not, have the codes read; ask about the fuel tank vent recall too.

issues.t: Blower motor or fan controller failure
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan stops working or only works on some speeds.
issues.why: The blower motor or the controller that sets its speed can fail.
issues.next: Have the blower and its controller tested; one or both may need replacing.

issues.t: Front sway bar link clunk
issues.sym: A knock or clunk from the front over bumps or rough roads.
issues.why: The sway bar end links and bushings wear out.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected; worn links are a quick, inexpensive fix.

issues.t: Tires wear unevenly from alignment
issues.sym: Tires wear on the edges early, or the car pulls slightly.
issues.why: Some owners report the alignment was off from new, causing premature tire wear.
issues.next: Get a four-wheel alignment and check tire wear again a few thousand miles later.

issues.t: Premium stereo amplifier pops or fails
issues.sym: Popping from the speakers, sudden volume jumps, or the sound cuts out.
issues.why: Suzuki issued a service bulletin for the premium sound system amplifier, and several owners had it replaced.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about the amplifier bulletin. A car audio shop can test the amplifier and subwoofer.

issues.t: Passenger seat trim panel breaks
issues.sym: The plastic trim on the side of the front passenger seat cushion comes loose or breaks at its clips.
issues.why: The retaining clips on this trim panel break easily; Suzuki later redesigned the part.
issues.next: A dealer or parts store can supply the newer trim piece.

issues.t: Paint chips easily and wheel finish peels
issues.sym: Many chips on the hood and front bumper, or spots and peeling on the wheels.
issues.why: Owners report thin paint that chips easily and wheel finishes that peel or stain.
issues.next: Touch up chips early to stop rust, and use mild wheel cleaners.
